chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent a sacrificial animal (hady) with a group of people, and appointed a day with them when they would yoke their sacrificial animal and enter into Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is prohibited upon him what is prohibited upon the one in Ihram on the day he appointed with them, until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination.'

So I said, 'What is your view if they delay in their appointed time and are slow in traveling with it? Is there blame upon him regarding the day which he appointed with them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and he is released (from Ihram) on the day which he appointed with them.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram
key_terms.هَدْيٍ: Sacrificial animal sent for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يُحْرِمُونَ: They enter into the state of Ihram
key_terms.يُقَلِّدُونَ: They yoke/prepare (specifically for the sacrificial animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Ihram prohibitions for someone who sends a sacrificial animal with a group but the animal is delayed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the temporal scope of Ihram prohibitions for a sender who dispatches a sacrificial animal (hady) with a group, establishing that the sender is bound by these restrictions only on the agreed-upon day of departure. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that if the group delays, the sender is released from the prohibitions for that specific day, highlighting the principle of conditional obligation based on the actual status of the sacrifice. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision in ritual timing and the distinction between the sender's personal state and the animal's journey.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazeyl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who sends a sacrificial animal with a group of people, and sets the timing with them when they were yoking their sacrificial animal in and they were wearing their Ihraam in. So heasws said: ‘It is Prohibited upon him what is Prohibited upon the one in Ihraam during the day when he fixed with them until the sacrificial animal reaches its place’.

So I said, ‘What is yourasws view if they lag behind in their fixed time, and are slower in the travelling, would there be blame upon him regarding the day which he fixed with them?’ Heasws said: ‘No, and he would free from Ihraam during the day which he fixed with them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who sends an animal for offering with a people, sets the time when they mark their animals for offering and assuming the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘At such time all things unlawful for them become unlawful for him until the animal for offering reaches its destination.’

I then asked, ‘What will happen if they cannot reach in the appointed time which is set up?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must not become as one not in the state of Ihram on the appointed day which he has set up with them.’”
